input: Set up a chore chart for the whole household

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of people, their ages, and roles (e.g. kids vs. adults) completely changes how chores are divided, how complex the chart needs to be, and whether ability levels must be factored in.
Knowing which specific chores to include (and exclude) determines the size and structure of the chart — a full deep-clean list looks very different from a daily basics list.
The type of home (house vs. apartment) and its size affects which chores even exist and how they should be grouped or split.
Time constraints per person and per chore (e.g. everyone is busy on weekdays) determine whether the chart is daily, weekly, or a mix, and how tasks are spaced out.
Whether the household prefers fixed assigned chores vs. a rotating system changes the entire logic of the chart and how fairness is perceived.
The format of the chart (physical poster, shared app, spreadsheet) determines how it will be created, displayed, and maintained long-term.
Understanding what 'working well' looks like — whether that's accountability, fairness, reduced conflict, or cleanliness standards — shapes how the chart is designed and enforced.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a chore chart for the household
gold.taskDescription: Create and implement a chore chart that assigns household tasks to all members of the home in an organised, fair, and sustainable way.

questions.title: How many people are in the household, and what are their ages?
questions.description: Identify the number of household members and their ages or life stages (e.g. young kids, teens, adults) to determine how chores should be divided and assigned.

questions.title: Which specific chores need to be on the chart?
questions.description: Define the list of chores to include — e.g. vacuuming, dishes, laundry, bins, bathrooms — and any that should be excluded or handled separately.

questions.title: What type and size of home are you managing chores for?
questions.description: Understand the home's layout and size to identify what areas and chore types are relevant (e.g. a large house with a garden is very different from a small apartment).

questions.title: Should the chart run on a daily, weekly, or mixed schedule?
questions.description: Determine the time cadence of the chart based on how often chores need to be done and when household members are realistically available.

questions.title: Do you want fixed assignments or a rotating system?
questions.description: Decide whether each person owns the same chores every week, or whether chores rotate among members to share the load more evenly over time.

questions.title: Where should the chart live — physical, app, or spreadsheet?
questions.description: Choose the format and tool for the chart (e.g. a printed wall chart, a shared app like Tody or OurHome, or a Google Sheets document) so it can be built and accessed by everyone.

questions.title: What does a successfully working chore chart look like to you?
questions.description: Clarify the end goal — whether it is reducing household conflict, ensuring a consistently clean home, teaching kids responsibility, or something else — to shape the design and rules of the chart.
